newsitem.title: THAILAND: Siam City Bank pays $47 mln on FRN put.
newsitem.headline: Siam City Bank pays $47 mln on FRN put.

text.p: Thai commercial lender Siam City Bank Plc paid $47 million to floating rate note (FRN) holders who exercised a put option on the bank's $50 million debt issue in June, a senior bank official said on Tuesday.
"Out of $50 million, $47 million was put," a senior member of the bank's treasury department told Reuters.
Note holders had told the bank of their intention to use the put at the start of June. The bank made payments to investors who exercised the put on June 19, the executive said.
The payment should not substantially affect the bank's position as it had a number of short term credit lines available, he said.
"Fortunately we have substantial bilateral lines which have not been utilised, but of course it is not long term," he said.
The bank was one of two large local lenders trying to arrange loans through foreign banks on Monday, market sources told Reuters.
"Next month we have six or seven loan maturities due so it is possible one of our dealers was in touch with one of our correspondent banks yesterday," the executive said.
The bank issued the $50 million FRN on June 17, 1994 through its Caymen Island branch. It has a five year term but the issue included a put option in the third year falling on June 17.

The note was arranged by Fuji Bank Luxembourg, the bank official said. Proceeds from the FRN had been loaned to clients using the Siam City Bank's Bangkok International Banking Facility (BIBF), he said.

The bank had no immediate plans to launch a replacement issue, he said. Siam City Bank Plc delayed issue of a $100 million Floating Rate Certificate of Deposit in March citing a Moody's Investors Service downgrade of Thailand's sovereign and bank sector credit ratings.
It has three other international floating rate or straight issues outstanding worth a combined $315 million.
